overview: Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral infection caused by the dengue virus (DENV), transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes. It is a leading cause of illness in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide.

types.name: Classic Dengue Fever
types.description: Mild to moderate fever with flu-like symptoms. Resolves in 7-10 days.

types.name: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF)
types.description: Severe form with bleeding, plasma leakage, and thrombocytopenia.

types.name: Dengue Shock Syndrome (DSS)
types.description: Life-threatening form with circulatory failure and shock.

causes: Dengue virus (4 serotypes: DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3, DENV-4)
Transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquito bite
Aedes albopictus (tiger mosquito) can also transmit
risk_factors: Living in or traveling to tropical/subtropical regions
Previous dengue infection (increases risk of severe dengue)
diagnosis: Complete Blood Count (CBC) — monitors platelets and WBC
PCR Test (most accurate, detects viral RNA)

general: Paracetamol for fever and pain (avoid NSAIDs and aspirin)
Hospitalization if platelets < 50,000/μL or severe symptoms
severe_cases: ICU care for dengue shock syndrome

prevention: Use mosquito nets and window screens
Dengue vaccine (Dengvaxia — for previously infected individuals)
emergency_signs: Bleeding from gums, nose, or in stool

faqs.question: Can dengue spread from person to person?
faqs.answer: No. Dengue spreads only through the bite of an infected Aedes mosquito, not through contact with an infected person.

faqs.question: Is dengue fatal?
faqs.answer: Classic dengue is rarely fatal. However, severe dengue (DHF/DSS) can be fatal without prompt medical treatment.
